title: Corrected Dual-Cavity Fabry-Perot Filter with Ge/ZnS Material Pair
scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using Germanium (high-index) and Zinc Sulfide (low-index) dielectric materials on CaF2 substrate can achieve high transmittance in both CO (4.55-4.75 μm) and CO2 (4.15-4.35 μm) bands while blocking 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm, with total layer count ≤24.
design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot filter with alternating quarter-wave Bragg reflectors separated by spacer cavities tuned to dual passband centers. Computational optimization adjusts layer thicknesses from quarter-wave initialization to achieve square passband profile with strong out-of-band blocking.
proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | Bragg reflector (6 layers Ge/ZnS) | Cavity spacer 1 (ZnS) | Bragg reflector (4 layers Ge/ZnS) | Cavity spacer 2 (ZnS) | Bragg reflector (6 layers Ge/ZnS) | Air, total 19 finite layers
soft_objectives: maximize average transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize average transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize average transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize average transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: conventional IR dielectric materials Ge and ZnS are depositable by thermal evaporation or sputtering
total film thickness should remain under 10 μm for stress management
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot interference condition: maximum transmittance when (φ1 + φ2 - 2δ)/2 = kπ
Quarter-wave stack reflectivity increases with layer pair count
Multi-cavity coupling shapes passband from triangular to square profile
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS pair has high index contrast (~4.0 vs ~2.2 in mid-IR) enabling fewer layers for required blocking
Dielectric-only design avoids metal absorption losses (15-30% reduction in transmittance)
19 layers leaves margin under 24-layer constraint for optimization flexibility
known_risks: Ge has absorption edge near 1.8 μm but should be transparent in 3.5-5.2 μm range - must verify dispersion model
Stress mismatch between Ge and ZnS may cause film cracking if total thickness exceeds practical limits
Fabrication tolerance sensitivity increases with layer count and index contrast
execution_request_english: Optimize a 19-layer dual-cavity Fabry-Perot infrared bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate. Layer stack: CaF2 | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | ZnS (cavity 1) | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | ZnS (cavity 2) | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Air. Use Germanium and Zinc Sulfide as dielectric materials with proper material registry identifiers. Initialize all layer thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness centered at 4.45 μm, then apply ±25% uniform bounds expansion for optimization search. Generate 50 candidate samples with disabled strict optical-margin pruning during candidate generation. Log which physical constraint filters reject candidates. Optimize for high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm bands, low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm bands. Normal incidence, air ambient. Report thicknesses_nm, best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and run_status. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
